x: Peter Bagnall was passed by Sando who also put up a new course record, but Jon also passed two himself and finished 3rd. Archie Bedford ran his usual "gutty" race and passed the Aylesford man putting Jack Brown off second 50 seconds behind Laurie Reed S.L.H. junior.

…he meeting generally was of a high standard and some excellent competition was seen, especially in the three miles with Sando and Norris running the whole distance together and finishing only inches apart in the wonderful time of 13 mins. 29.8 secs. which at that time was only 3.4secs outside the wo…
Archie Bedford ran well over the 4th stage but quite naturally was unable to cope with record runs by Norris and Sando and was relegated to 8th place.

Knight of Essex Beagles was the individual winner completing the course in record time and finishing in front of Sando. Pete Bagnall was our first man home in 11th position and supported by Masters, Short and L.
Minor placings were gained by Jack Brown who was 2nd to Sando in the three miles; Charlie Jones was second to Wilmshurst in the Triple jump.
Charlie Dabbs,on the long leg from Mitcham to Purley,had the misfortune to start only a few seconds ahead of Ken Caulder of Surrey, Sando, and Towl of H.H.H.

It should also be recorded that other notabilities on this stage were Sando, Driver, Heatley, O'Gorman, Keily and Ingles, all of whom beat the previous record and all of whom gained assistance in battling with the opposition.
Young Alan Black, undeterred by the star names around him, ran a very sensible 3rd stage, dropping places only to Sando and O'Gorman, each of whom broke the course record.

At six miles, Eldon had established a substantial lead from Knight and Sando with Maynard 4th. Our lads had shewn considerable improvement in their team placings and were steadily pulling back the opposition with six men now in 87 and eight in 126.
… - Hyman, Peter Cl[illegible]rk, Brian Fernee, Chapman, Roath, Perkins, Mike Barratt, George Brown, Maynard, Palmer and Sando just to mention a few are not designed to rouse one's confidence.…
